Here is my medical report, can you analyze it and tell me when I need to see the doctor next? 

Patient Name: Vince Kamniski
DOB: 14 March 1990
Report Date: 28 November 2025
Provider: Dr. Elena Moretti, MD, 
Doctor's Email: moretti@northshoregeneral.com
Clinic: North Shore General Internal Medicine

Reason for Visit: Annual physical examination and routine health screening.

Medical History: Past medical history includes mild seasonal allergic rhinitis and a remote ankle sprain (2021, resolved). No past surgeries. Medications include Loratadine 10 mg as needed. No known drug allergies. Family history: father with hypertension (age 52), mother with hypothyroidism.

Social History: Software engineer. Non-smoker. Alcohol: 2–4 drinks per week socially. Exercises 3–4 times per week (running and weight training). Balanced diet with moderate red-meat intake. Sleep averages 6.5–7 hours nightly.

Vital Signs: Blood Pressure 118/76 mmHg; Heart Rate 68 bpm; Respiratory Rate 14 breaths/min; Temperature 36.6°C; Height 181 cm; Weight 83 kg; BMI 25.3.

Physical Examination: Well-appearing male, no acute distress. Cardiovascular: normal S1/S2, no murmurs. Lungs: clear bilaterally. Abdomen: soft, non-tender. Neurological: alert and oriented, normal strength and reflexes. Musculoskeletal: full range of motion. Skin: no suspicious lesions.

Laboratory Results: CBC within normal limits (WBC 5.8, Hemoglobin 15.2 g/dL, Platelets 245). Metabolic panel normal (Sodium 140, Potassium 4.2, Creatinine 0.98 mg/dL, eGFR 104, AST 22, ALT 26). Lipid panel: Total Cholesterol 191 mg/dL, LDL 118 mg/dL, HDL 54 mg/dL, Triglycerides 112 mg/dL. HbA1c 5.2%.

Assessment: Generally healthy adult male. LDL cholesterol slightly elevated. Allergic rhinitis stable.

Plan: Continue regular exercise. Increase dietary fiber, reduce saturated fats to target LDL <100 mg/dL. Recommend dermatology screening every 2 years. Continue Loratadine as needed. Follow up annually.
steps.expected_behavior: Agent should analyze the medical report and decide whether the user needs to visit the doctor soon or not
steps.agent_response:
Summary — quick interpretation
- Overall: You’re generally healthy based on this annual exam. Vitals, exam, CBC and metabolic panel are all normal. HbA1c (5.2%) and eGFR are normal.
- Main abnormality: LDL cholesterol mildly elevated at 118 mg/dL (goal per the plan <100 mg/dL for primary prevention).

What this means and recommended next steps
1. Short-term (recommended now)
   - Lifestyle first: follow the plan — increase fiber, reduce saturated fat, continue exercise and weight maintenance. These are appropriate first steps for LDL 118.
   - Repeat fasting lipid panel in ~3 months (around late Feb 2026 given the 28 Nov 2025 report) to see if lifestyle changes lower the LDL. This is a common and reasonable interval.

2. When to see the doctor next
   - Primary care follow-up: Annual visit — next routine appointment in ~1 year (around late Nov 2026), as already recommended in the report.
   - Earlier visit: Schedule sooner if you develop symptoms (chest pain, unexplained shortness of breath, new neurological symptoms, suspicious skin lesion, or other concerns) or if you want to review medications sooner.
   - Lipid-focused visit: Consider a brief follow-up or phone/telehealth visit at the time of the repeat lipid test (in ~3 months) if results are still above target or if you want to discuss medication options then.
   - Dermatology: Recommended screening every 2 years — next dermatology screen ~Nov 2027 unless you notice a suspicious lesion sooner.

3. When medication might be considered
   - Given your age (~35), normal BP, non-smoker status, normal HbA1c, and current lipid values, your 10-year ASCVD risk is likely low and starting a statin is not routinely indicated right now. If repeat lipids remain elevated (for example LDL persistently ≥130 mg/dL or LDL ≥100 mg/dL with other risk factors or a rising risk estimate), discuss statin therapy with Dr. Moretti.

4. Other routine items to keep in mind
   - Continue annual influenza vaccine and review other immunizations as needed.
   - Consider repeating diabetes screening (A1c) every 2–3 years given current normal result unless risk factors change.
   - Keep monitoring blood pressure and lifestyle metrics.

Minor note
- The report lists the patient name as “Vince Kamniski” (missing an 'n'). Do you want me to confirm/correct that with Dr. Moretti before any scheduling?

Would you like me to:
- Draft or send an email to Dr. Elena Moretti to schedule a 3-month lipid recheck and/or a 1-year follow-up? (I can include your preferred signature: "Best regards, Vince Kaminski.")
- Book a dermatology referral?
- Calculate a formal 10-year ASCVD risk (I can do that if you tell me your race)?
